items.title: Scammers Are Cashing In on a Real Government Refund — Don't Fall for It
items.summary: A real refund program is sending money to people who got signed up for a subscription they didn't want — and crooks are already using the news to trick folks out of their bank details. The Federal Trade Commission says it will never call, text, or email you to offer a refund, and never asks you to pay a fee to collect. If you get a message about money you're owed, that's a scam. Don't reply and don't click. Go to ftc.gov/refunds and look up the program yourself.

items.title: Criminals are selling scans of 153 million driver's licenses — freeze your credit free with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion
items.summary: A dark-web service is selling digital scans of more than 153 million driver's licenses from the U.S. and Canada, and the FBI has opened an investigation. You can't un-leak a license, but you can lock your credit so nobody opens a loan or a card in your name. Go to equifax.com, experian.com, and transunion.com, sign up for a free account, and click Freeze — do all three, because it's free by law and takes about ten minutes total. If you'd rather see your reports first, go to annualcreditreport.com, the one government-approved site for free reports.

items.title: Windows 11's Recall takes a picture of your screen every few seconds — turn it off free in Settings > Privacy & security > Recall & snapshots
items.summary: On newer "Copilot+" Windows 11 computers, a feature called Recall quietly saves snapshots of everything on your screen so you can search your own history later. Most people never turned it on and never agreed to it. To check: click Start, type Recall & snapshots, and open Settings > Privacy & security > Recall & snapshots. Turn off Save snapshots — or click Pause and delete what's already saved. If the setting isn't there, your computer simply doesn't have it, and you're done.

items.title: That 'Your Parcel Couldn't Be Delivered — Pay $4.95' Message Is Fake
items.summary: A fresh batch of fake messages says a parcel couldn't be delivered and you owe about five dollars to get it moving. The link opens a page that copies the post office's official look, then asks for your name, your phone number, and finally your bank card. That's an email scam, not a shipping notice. The real Postal Service, UPS, and FedEx never text a link for a small fee. Don't click — open the carrier's real website and check your tracking number there.

items.title: Your computer's drive can warn you before it quits — Windows 11 shows its free health report in Settings > System > Storage
items.summary: Click Start, type Storage, and open Storage settings. Then click Advanced storage settings, then Disks & volumes, click the drive your files live on, click Properties, and read the Drive health line. If it says Healthy, you're fine. If it says Caution or Bad, that drive is on its way out — copy what you can't lose onto something else today, not next month.

items.title: Windows 11's free September update lets you move the taskbar to the top of the screen and shut Bing off in Search — get it at Settings > Windows Update
items.summary: Install it from Settings > Windows Update and restart. Then, to move the taskbar: Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors > Taskbar position, and pick Left, Top, Right, or Bottom. There's also a smaller taskbar size in that same section if the bar feels too tall. To stop the Start menu from covering half your screen: Settings > Personalization > Start > Start menu size, and choose Small. To make Search instant and quiet: Settings > Privacy & security > Search, open Show suggested search results, and turn off Web Searches and Microsoft Store suggestions.

items.title: Those 'Your Rewards Points Are Expiring' Texts Are Fake
items.summary: A wave of fake text messages is telling people their rewards points are about to expire, with a believable balance and a deadline to make it feel urgent. The link inside opens a fake sign-in page that steals your email address and password. Researchers counted more than a thousand versions of the same message. Don't use the link. Open the company's official website instead by typing its address into your browser, then sign in there and check for yourself.

items.title: Stop ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude from training their AI on your chats — three free settings, about two minutes each
items.summary: In ChatGPT, open Settings → Data Controls and turn off Improve the model for everyone. In Gemini, open Settings and turn off Keep Activity (or go to myactivity.google.com and turn off Gemini Apps Activity). In Claude, open Settings → Privacy and turn off the model improvement setting. Nothing breaks when you do this and nothing costs money — you keep using the app exactly as before, and your conversations stop feeding the next version of it.

items.title: Update Firefox free to get a PDF reader that opens up to 45% faster — click Menu, then Help, then About Firefox
items.summary: The newest Firefox came out September 15, and Mozilla says the PDF reader built into it now starts up to 45% faster, with a big drop in memory and processor use when a page is showing large photos. To get it: open Firefox, click the Menu button (the three lines in the top right corner), then Help, then About Firefox. It checks and installs the newest version for free, and your tabs, bookmarks, and saved passwords all stay exactly where they are.

items.title: That Antivirus Renewal Email Is Fake — Check Your Bank Statement First
items.summary: Scammers are emailing people a convincing receipt that says their antivirus subscription just auto-renewed for about $130, with a handy link to cancel it. There is no subscription and no charge. The cancel page is a fake form that collects your name, email address and number so a fake support agent can call you next. Don't click the link and don't fill in that form. Check your own bank statement instead — no charge means nothing to cancel.

items.title: Is your Windows 11 computer about to stop getting free security updates? Microsoft's October 13 deadline takes 30 seconds to check in Settings
items.summary: On October 13, Microsoft stops sending free security updates to the older version of Windows 11 that shipped back in 2024. The fix is free and it's just an update: open Settings > Windows Update, click Check for updates, and install everything it offers — your files and programs stay exactly where they are. Not sure which version you have? Press the Start button and type About your PC; it's written right there in plain text.

items.title: Columbia County's library pays for Career Online High School — a free, accredited high school diploma you finish from your kitchen table
items.summary: Call the Columbia County Public Library at (386) 758-2111 and ask about Career Online High School. It's a real, accredited high school diploma plus a career certificate, done entirely online at your own pace, and the grant pays the whole cost — you don't pay a dime. The library has a page with the enrollment steps on columbiacountyfla.com (search "Career Online High School" on the site).
